2607.11357.title: OpsMem: Dual-Memory Reasoning with Cross-Memory Resonance for Failure Diagnosis
2607.11357.paper_summary: Failure diagnosis in modern software systems requires iterative evidence acquisition and hypothesis reasoning guided by operational experience. Existing LLM-based methods improve diagnosis through agentic reasoning or knowledge augmentation, but they often lack a mechanism to coordinate the evolving diagnostic state with operational experience during iterative diagnosis. We propose OpsMem, a dual-memory framework that maintains a short-term memory for the current diagnostic state and a long-term memory for reusable operational experience. OpsMem uses cross-memory resonance to activate state-relevant long-term memory, conditions multi-agent diagnosis on the short-term and activated long-term memories, and consolidates reusable experience from solved incidents back into long-term memory. Experiments on a real-world Huawei microservice failure diagnosis dataset show that OpsMem outperforms representative agentic-reasoning and knowledge-augmented baselines, improving Match and Relevant by up to 46.88% and 18.39% over the strongest baseline, respectively.
2607.11357.paper_summary_zh: 現代軟體系統中的故障診斷需要迭代的證據獲取和由操作經驗指導的假設推理。現有的基於LLM的方法通過代理推理或知識增強來改善診斷，但它們通常缺乏一種機制來在迭代診斷過程中協調不斷演變的診斷狀態與操作經驗。我們提出了OpsMem，一個雙記憶框架，維護當前診斷狀態的短期記憶和可重用操作經驗的長期記憶。OpsMem使用跨記憶共鳴來激活與狀態相關的長期記憶，基於短期和激活的長期記憶進行多代理診斷，並將已解決事件的可重用經驗整合回長期記憶中。對於一個真實的華為微服務故障診斷數據集的實驗顯示，OpsMem在代表性的代理推理和知識增強基準上表現更佳，分別提高了Match和Relevant的表現，最高可達46.88%和18.39%。
